turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Afternoon. You look done in. Come sit, what's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I'm tired, can we just get on with it. My hands go dead at night.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, man. Tell me a bit more, however it comes.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Right hand. At night the thumb, the index and the middle finger go numb, pins and needles, and I shake the hand to wake it up. It's been three weeks... no, six weeks.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And he's dropping cups. I picked two up off the kitchen floor this week.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja the cups, mostly the right. They just slip. I'm not being clumsy on purpose.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Is it only at night, or on shift as well?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The dead feeling is at night. If I grip the press it tingles, but that's not the same as waking up with it dead.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He shakes it over the bed. Wakes me. Nearly every night.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja well the plant is hectic. Night shift at the fittings plant, then this on top. I sat at a red robot this morning just staring.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): That drive sounds rough. Any pain in the hand, or is it just the numb feeling?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really pain. Sometimes an ache in the wrist after, nothing much.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any fever in the last while?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): And a cough? Anything on the chest?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has your weight shifted?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm I don't know. Maybe. The trousers still fit, I haven't been on a scale, so I can't really say.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, we leave that. What are you taking, medicine-wise?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodopine for the pressure. Five milligrams... no, they put me up, it's 10 milligrams in the morning.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol one at night, 20 milligrams. Don't ask me the proper name.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar tablets, one with breakfast. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, a spoon mixed in water, from the shop.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He mixes that brown powder every morning. Doesn't skip it.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Let me see the hands. No swelling at either wrist.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll tap the right wrist now.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Eish. Ja, it shoots into those fingers.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Tapping the wrist brings the tingling on. Thumb muscle isn't wasted, that looks fine.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thumb, index and middle at night, and that tap. It sounds like carpal tunnel, the nerve getting pinched at the wrist. Working impression, not a final diagnosis.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): So what now? The foreman's already on my case, I can't be booking off.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wear a wrist splint at night while you sleep. The right one for sure, and both hands if you've got a pair.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): A splint. Fine. Is that the whole plan?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the numbness hasn't eased when I see you again, we'll book a nerve conduction test. Not today, only if it hasn't settled.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): And the appointment? I don't want to sit in that waiting room for nothing.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): In six weeks. Reception will book it, that's fixed.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll put the splint where he can see it. He leaves half his things in the bakkie.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag alright. Are we done? I'm shattered.

spec.situation: Middle-aged office or factory worker with night-time numbness in thumb, index and middle fingers, shakes hands to wake them; dropping cups; splint advice, nerve test conditional.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

bad.reason: Dropping cups supported, but right-hand detail is only 'mostly the right,' not exclusively right hand.
bad.text: Dropping cups (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, body_site=right hand, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Possible diabetes history implied by current 'sugar tablets, one with breakfast' is not recorded in past medical history.
Weight change was asked about and the patient was unsure/could not say whether weight had changed; this uncertainty is not recorded.
No significant hand pain was reported; patient said 'not really pain', only sometimes a mild wrist ache after. The negative response to hand pain being largely absent is not recorded.
The nocturnal numbness occurs nearly every night, per caregiver report, which is not recorded.

Excessive tiredness/shatteredness was described by the patient ('I'm tired', 'I'm shattered'), including impaired alertness while driving ('sat at a red robot this morning just staring'); this is not recorded.
